results.corrected_title: OpenAI launches Daybreak Red Team and Defense Factory security products
results.corrected_summary: At a keynote on 2026-11-12, OpenAI President Greg Brockman presented two products on OpenAI's Daybreak security platform. Daybreak Red Team (early access) uses AI agents to test companies' web applications for vulnerabilities and to validate reported flaws and patches. Daybreak Defense Factory uses agents running on the GPT-6 Cyber model to scan codebases, find vulnerabilities and draft merge-ready pull requests with a test, which engineers review before production.
key_facts: Launched at a keynote by Greg Brockman on 2026-11-12
Daybreak Red Team is in early access and runs continuous pen-testing of web applications
Daybreak Defense Factory automates finding, validating and fixing vulnerabilities
GPT-6 Cyber currently powers Defense Factory's agents
Engineers review and approve patches before production
results.issues: Single primary-quality source; GPT-6 Cyber itself predates the window.

results.corrected_title: OpenAI launches Businesses in ChatGPT beta with verified Business Agents and Business Hub
results.corrected_summary: On 2026-11-10 OpenAI began a beta of 'Businesses in ChatGPT'. Verified Business Agents let users chat with a brand, usually after a participating company appears in a ChatGPT answer. These chats are labeled and kept separate from the user's main conversation. Companies claim and verify their organization in a Business Hub, which reportedly shows how often they are mentioned in ChatGPT responses. The beta is limited to eligible US e-commerce and online service businesses.
key_facts: Business Agent chats are labeled and kept separate from the main conversation
Business Hub is where companies claim and verify their organization
Limited to eligible US e-commerce and online service businesses
results.issues: OpenAI's own announcement not opened; several secondary outlets agree.

results.corrected_title: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Robotics 2.5 and AlphaGenome 2
results.corrected_summary: Google DeepMind announced Gemini Robotics 2.5 and AlphaGenome 2 on 2026-11-11, though one outlet says 2026-11-10 for the robotics model. DeepMind reports a 96% success rate in a Mercedes-Benz proof-of-concept on active production lines. AlphaGenome 2 identifies causal variants at 30% on the TenK10K benchmark versus 16% for the previous approach.
key_facts: Gemini Robotics 2.5 reached 96% in a Mercedes-Benz proof-of-concept, a figure DeepMind itself reports
Rolling out to partners including Apptronik, Agile Robots and Boston Dynamics, with no public API
On TenK10K, causal variant identification was 30% versus 16% before
AlphaGenome 2 available through the API for non-commercial research
results.issues: Vendor-reported figures; DeepMind blog not opened.
